--- title: "Introduction to Quarto — Lab" subtitle: "RaukR 2026 · Day 1" author: "" date: "" --- ::: {.callout-note} ## Scope Build one penguins document with the authoring extras, then **cite it** and render it as a **branded Typst PDF**. Two challenges, one document — each is its own hands-on part, with the between-parts break in between. This is your **manuscript / team-project path** — the same route from an analysis to a submittable write-up. Everything runs on **base-R `datasets::penguins`** (R ≥ 4.5) — no data to download. **Packages:** `dplyr`, `ggplot2`, `gt`, `ggokabeito` (a colour-blind-safe palette — see the Accessibility box below), plus the `knitr`/`rmarkdown` engine every `.qmd` with R code needs. If you've done the **[Setup page](../../setup.qmd)** (with its one-command `quarto check`), you're ready; otherwise install them once from R: `install.packages(c("dplyr", "ggplot2", "gt", "ggokabeito"))`. The citation payoff also uses the shared `references.bib` and `apa.csl` shipped in this folder. ::: Start every document with this setup — the challenges below assume it: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(dplyr) library(ggplot2) library(gt) library(ggokabeito) # colour-blind-safe (Okabe-Ito) scale -- see the Accessibility box data(penguins) penguins <- penguins |> filter(!is.na(bill_len), !is.na(bill_dep)) ``` ::: ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Coming from R Markdown? (2-minute aside — optional) You do **not** need to convert anything to work natively in Quarto — start with `.qmd` directly. But if you have an `.Rmd` you want to bring over: - it renders **as-is** — Quarto reads `.Rmd` too; - cell options move from the chunk header to the `#|` "hash-pipe" (one YAML option per line); - `knitr::convert_chunk_header("doc.Rmd", output = "doc.qmd")` does the mechanical part. That's the whole migration. The rest of this lab is native `.qmd`. ::: ## Authoring Challenge > **Goal:** a penguins report with a cross-referenced **figure**, a cross-referenced **table**, a > **margin** element, and a display **equation** — rendered to HTML. ::: {.callout-note icon=false} ## {{< fa clipboard-list >}} Tasks 1. Create a new `.qmd` **inside `labs/quarto/`** in your cloned repo (next to `references.bib` / `apa.csl`, so Part 2's paths and branding resolve later) with `format: html` and the setup cell at the top of this page. 2. Add a scatter plot of `bill_len` versus `bill_dep` colored by `species`. Give its cell `#| label: fig-bill` and a `#| fig-cap:`, then — **in the prose, outside the cell** — refer to it with `@fig-bill`. 3. Add a summary table. The `gt` plumbing is below; your job is the **cross-reference mechanic** — give the cell `#| label: tbl-summary` and a `#| tbl-cap:`, then refer to it with `@tbl-summary`. ```r penguins |> summarise(bill_len = mean(bill_len), bill_dep = mean(bill_dep), .by = species) |> gt() ``` 4. Put the species counts in the **margin** with the cell option `#| column: margin`. 5. *(stretch)* Add the bill-shape ratio as a display equation, referenced with `@eq-ratio`. **Escape the underscores** — inside `$$…$$`, `bill_len` may render as a subscript (depending on the math renderer), so write: ```markdown $$ \text{ratio} = \frac{\text{bill\_len}}{\text{bill\_dep}} $$ {#eq-ratio} ``` 6. Render to HTML (`quarto render your-doc.qmd`, or the editor's Render/Preview). ::: ::: {.callout-tip icon=false} ## {{< fa universal-access >}} Make it accessible The worked report does all three — do the same in yours: - add a `#| fig-alt:` to every figure; - add `scale_color_okabe_ito()` (from `ggokabeito`) to your plot, keeping `shape = species`; - add `axe: {output: document}` under `format: html`, re-preview, and a WCAG report appears on the page (drop it again before you publish). See [Quarto's accessibility docs](https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/html-accessibility.html). ::: ::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false} ## {{< fa circle-check >}} You should see A numbered **Figure 1** (the bill scatter, three separate clusters), a numbered **Table 1**, the counts sitting in the right margin, and an **Equation 1** — with `@fig-bill` / `@tbl-summary` / `@eq-ratio` rendering as live "Figure 1" / "Table 1" / "Equation 1" links. Your finished figure looks like this: ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Target: bill length versus depth by species.](index_files/figure-html/fig-target-1.png){#fig-target fig-alt='Scatter plot of bill depth against bill length for three penguin species in distinct colors; the species form largely separate clusters.' width=576} ::: ::: ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Hint - A cell becomes a cross-referenceable figure/table only when its label **starts with** `fig-` / `tbl-` / `eq-` and is **unique** in the document. - `column: margin` is a **cell option** (`#|`) for a cell, or a `::: {.column-margin}` div for prose. - Display math with a label: `$$ … $$ {#eq-ratio}` — reference it with `@eq-ratio`. ::: **The complete, runnable solution is `starter.qmd`** — a known-good Part-1 report with all these cells. Open it from your cloned `labs/quarto/` to compare, or take the source: {{< fa download >}} starter.qmd The cross-references and the equation live in the **body Markdown**, outside any cell: ``` markdown @fig-bill shows bill shape by species; @tbl-summary gives the per-species means. $$ \text{ratio} = \frac{\text{bill\_len}}{\text{bill\_dep}} $$ {#eq-ratio} ``` **[`penguins-report.qmd`](penguins-report.qmd) is a reference, not a checklist.** The complete worked document goes beyond the tasks (a margin culmen figure, a `glimpse`, section labels) and also adds the citations from the next challenge. Prefer to open the whole thing in your editor? Take the source: {{< fa download >}} penguins-report.qmd ## Citations Challenge > **Goal:** cite the report, then render the *same document* as a **branded Typst PDF** — the > manuscript payoff, no LaTeX. ::: {.callout-note} ## Starting point If you finished the Authoring Challenge, keep going on your own document. Otherwise open **`labs/quarto/starter.qmd`** in your editor — a known-good Part-1 report — and add the citations to that. Nobody is stranded by the break. ::: ::: {.callout-note icon=false} ## {{< fa clipboard-list >}} Tasks 1. Point the document header at the shared bibliography and citation style: ```yaml bibliography: references.bib csl: apa.csl ``` 2. Cite the data source in prose with `@gorman2014`. Find (or add) the sentence ending *"…collected at Palmer Station, Antarctica."* and insert the citation before the period: `Antarctica [@gorman2014].` (don't paste a second copy). 3. Add a **References** section where the list should appear: ```markdown ## References {.unnumbered} ::: {#refs} ::: ``` 4. Give it a real **title block** so the PDF reads as a paper — **replace** your document's `author:` line with: ```yaml author: - name: Your Name affiliation: Your Lab, Your University ``` 5. Render to HTML and confirm the citation resolves to *(Gorman et al., 2014)* with a formatted reference list. 6. Switch the output to **Typst** and render a branded PDF. *(Heads-up: you'll see a stack of `unknown font family` warnings as it renders — they're harmless; the Troubleshooting box below explains them.)* Two routes: - **CLI** — leave the header as-is and force the target: ```bash quarto render your-doc.qmd --to typst ``` - **Editor Render button** — set `format: typst` in the YAML header first, *then* click Render. The button renders whatever `format:` is declared, so while the header still says `format: html` the button gives you HTML, **not** a PDF. Where the PDF lands: rendering the shipped `starter.qmd` writes the PDF under `_site/…` (it's in the site's render list); a brand-new doc renders the PDF next to its source. ::: ::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false} ## {{< fa circle-check >}} You should see In-text **(Gorman et al., 2014)**, a **References** section formatted in APA, and — in the Typst PDF — the same citation and reference list, typeset with the RaukR palette. No `?@gorman2014` or `[?]` markers anywhere. ::: ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Hint - The `@key` in `[@gorman2014]` must match a key in `references.bib` **exactly**. - `csl:` sets the style (here APA). Swap the file to restyle every citation at once. - Typst reads the `.bib` itself, so keep bibliography fields plain — avoid LaTeX macros like `\emph{}` in titles. - On the first Typst render, Quarto downloads the brand's Google fonts; give it a moment and a network connection. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true" code-summary="Solution — the header and the cite"} # In the YAML header: # bibliography: references.bib # csl: apa.csl # # In prose: # The data come from Palmer Station, Antarctica [@gorman2014]. # # A References section (the list renders inside the #refs div): # ## References {.unnumbered} # ::: {#refs} # ::: # # For the branded PDF (the project _brand.yml styles it), either force the target from the CLI: # quarto render your-doc.qmd --to typst # or set `format: typst` in the header and use the editor's Render button. ``` ::: The complete cited HTML is [`penguins-report.qmd`](penguins-report.qmd); the branded Typst PDF — with R-side `theme_brand_*` styling — is [`sample-typst.qmd`](sample-typst.qmd) (the link opens the rendered PDF, not a web page). ## Troubleshooting ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" icon=false} ## {{< fa wrench >}} If a render misbehaves - **YAML is indentation-sensitive.** If rendering fails *before* any code runs, check the YAML header for stray spaces, tabs, or unmatched quotes. - **Missing package?** `install.packages("")` (or `renv::restore()`) and render again. - **A figure doesn't appear?** Check the path is relative to the `.qmd` and the filename matches exactly (case included). - **A cross-reference shows `?@…`?** The cell label must start with `fig-`/`tbl-`/`eq-` and be unique, and the `@ref` must match it. - **A citation shows `?@gorman2014` or `[?]`?** The `@key` doesn't match a key in `references.bib`, or `bibliography:` isn't set. - **Do I need to install Typst?** No — Typst is bundled in Quarto ≥ 1.9, so there's nothing extra to install (no LaTeX either); check `quarto --version`. - **Typst PDF looks unbranded / wrong fonts?** Confirm `_brand.yml` is at the project root and you have network on the first render (Quarto fetches the Google fonts once). - **Typst prints `unknown font family` warnings?** Harmless — a plain `gt` table emits them for its default font stack; the PDF still builds. (The fully brand-styled table via `theme_brand_*` is in `sample-typst.qmd`.) - **Prefer to stay in HTML first?** Render HTML, get it right, *then* switch to `format: typst` — the content is the same. :::
